segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin, including one managing cystic acne, report the formula suits them well — one notes her oiliness likely helps offset the product's inherently drying texture, and another reports smoother, brighter skin with fewer breakouts and faded old scarring.
segments.dry: A reviewer with dry skin pairs the emulsion with a separate moisturizer to offset its inherently dry, non-greasy texture, reporting it stays supple and produces visible flaking as her skin turns over.
segments.mature: Reviewers framing this for older or more visibly aging skin report it as especially effective for their age group, citing softened dark spots, reduced fine lines, and one calling it "the magic key for older skin."

concerns.aging: Reviewers report smoother texture, fewer visible fine lines, and a more even, radiant complexion with consistent use over several weeks to months, with several noting mature or older skin sees more dramatic benefit than younger skin.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers report the formula is non-greasy and either maintains or doesn't worsen hydration, though it is described as an inherently dry, fast-absorbing texture; a couple of reviewers note temporary tightness or dryness right after application, and one long-time retinoid user isn't sure the product is fully absorbing rather than sitting on top of her skin.
concerns.redness: Reviewers report no new redness from the product itself, and several specifically credit it with reducing the redness of existing acne scars, including ones several months old.
concerns.barrier: Most reviewers, including some switching from stronger prescription retinoids, report no irritation, peeling, or breakouts even with frequent use; one reviewer notes the product will "purge" skin as a normal adjustment phase before results appear.
concerns.spots: Many reviewers report fading of dark spots, hyperpigmentation, old acne scarring, and even old chicken-pox scars with consistent use, generally noticed within a few weeks.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers managing acne, including cystic acne, report fewer breakouts and faster-resolving blemishes, with one saying acne now disappears almost as soon as it appears; one reviewer specifically credits it with reducing red acne scars, including older ones.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer with somewhat oily skin reports her oiliness likely helps offset what she expects would otherwise be a drying formula.

extraits.titre: It feels nice but I’m not sure it sinks in
extraits.texte: I’ve been using retinol and retinoids for years so I can’t tell if this is “working” yet. It’s a nice texture and dries pretty quickly. It is yellow in color which is normal, however, when I wake up in the morning and use toner to clean my face, my cotton pad is covered in yellow. Which makes me wonder if this even sinks in. And, if it doesn’t sink in, is it able to work properly? I’m not sure. But I will continue to use until I finish the bottle and see how I feel then.

extraits.titre: Takes a little time, like any OTC retinoid, but it's incredible.Takes a little time, like any OTC retinoid, but it's inc
extraits.texte: I was a retinoid latecomer, in fact a latecomer to skincare as a whole, not doing anything special until I was 40. By then some damage had already appeared in the form of noticeably thinning skin (I saw capillaries scattered around my face, and this made me look older than any other sign of aging I was experiencing), fine lines, and discolored spots. I wanted to get on the strongest things I could as soon as possible. I began with The Ordinary's Granactive Retinoid 2% emulsion, because I'd read it was a beginner-friendly gentle option, but I had the goal of jumping to this retinaldehyde emulsion all along. I'm not 28, after all! (I need to emphasize that middle-aged and older women will see more benefits from strong retinoids like this than younger women, like under 35. Y'all have good enough skin that the changes you'll see are less extreme than what we'll see.) My skin is not sensitive, so I was able to upgrade to this retinal just 6 months after using the granactive. I now use it 6 nights out of 7 with no irritation. The 7th night is exfoliation. I'm not saying everyone will be able to do that, but this is gentle enough - in contrast with conventional retinol - that you might. I have somewhat oily skin, which helps; I expect it'd be drying otherwise, and I do have to put on extra moisturizer in the winter. (But don't we all?) I also apply sunscreen to my face every single day without exception. If you use retinoids and you don't do that, you'll regret it and you won't see

The results, quite frankly, left me astonished. I'm a 32 year old male, cystic acne, oily skin, small pours, large hair follicles. I've been going between different retinoid products for several months now, with decent results. I just recently switched to The Ordinary's Retinal, and here's my experience. This stuff is so good, that even two old chicken pock scars from my childhood are significantly faded. For my skin type, it's perfect. I use a very light weight birch sap moisturizer after applying, along with this company's niacinamide, and it simply works magic. My skin feels smoother, is brighter, and way less prone to breakouts. My face rarely sees anything unless I get razor burn. The only con I can think of is that it stains clothes, and makes you look like you're covered in mustard.

Been using this nightly for 12 nights. I have been using generous amounts — 3 full pumps — one each for my face, neck and the backs of my hands. I'm surprised the small quantity in the bottle has lasted this long. Absorption isn't great; it's a very dry formula. I seriously don't know how people get by with "pea sized" amounts. Applying it to damp skin isn't really effective for me as far as assisting with absorption; despite finishing with a damp washcloth, my face is already too dry by the time I reach for the bottle. After applying the retinal, I mist my face with water and it significantly assists with spreadability and absorption. I get a nice tingle, too. As appropriate for retinal, there is no fragrance to note. I pair the retinal with Neutrogena Ultra Gentle moisturizing cream which contains CICA and B5. It's lightweight, sufficiently moisturizing for my dry skin and leaves it supple. Nice texture and absorbs beautifully. The CICA counteracts any irritation I might experience from the retinal, and I got a huge 11 oz jar for $10. It was really a steal. Once my skin adjusts to the retinal, though, I will likely move on to something with niacinamide and peptides. As stated, this is a dry formula so it is totally non-greasy. It's hard to tell how much it has improved my skin thus far, but I am getting lots of flaking which is what I wanted. I have no doubt I will see a significant difference once that outer layer of dead skin cells have all turned over and expect further

I’m supposed to take it once a week and I was taking it every night show it pays to read the directions lol This is the magic key for older skin

Don't let the small size fool you. I ordered this April 5th (109 days ago) and started with the recommended 2x a week and quickly worked my way up to every other day. Sometimes I'll even use two pumps instead of one. I still haven't used it up! Not only have I gotten tons of uses out of it, but I've also experienced ZERO irritation. I was worried about starting a retinoid because I've heard they can be irritating and take a while to get used to. I haven't had a single issue using this product. My acne disappears almost as soon as it shows up, and I've noticed pretty good improvement in my hyperpigmentation. I'm going to continue using this product for the foreseeable future.

I've been using this for about 2 weeks now, 2–3 times a week, and so far it's been okay. It comes in a small pump bottle that's easy to use. The product is yellowish in colour, applies nicely on skin, and although it's only 15 ml, you only need a small amount so it should last a while. Before this, I was using 1% Retinol in Squalane. When I first started using retinol, I had breakouts and peeling even though I introduced it gradually. I was a bit worried about switching to this, but thankfully I've had no redness/peeling, or breakouts so far. My skin doesn't feel dry either. If you're new to retinoids, I'd recommend starting with a lower strength before trying this one. I haven't noticed any dramatic results yet, but it's only been a couple of weeks, and I know these products take time to work.
